title: Introduce RBACv2 attribute filter, KMS geo-fallback middleware, and audit redaction shim
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: customer audits and internal compliance reviews highlighted two gaps: (1) RBACv2 policies allow attribute-driven grants, but there is no safe filtering step to drop unsafe operator attributes from policy evaluation; (2) KMS-based key operations need a deterministic, auditable fallback when a region-preferred KMS is unreachable so we can maintain availability without violating data-residency commitments. Additionally, audit logs must be redacted to remove high-risk PII while preserving regional-residency tags and integrity checks. This PR adds an attribute-filter pass to the RBACv2 compiler, a KMS geo-fallback middleware that prefers regional CMKs and falls back to approved provider pool with explicit consent flags, and an audit redaction shim that strips sensitive fields while injecting canonical residency metadata and HMAC anchors for non-repudiation.

merge_summary: Merged via squash on 2024-10-22 after CI green. Key points: attribute-filter is behind a namespace opt-in feature flag; KMS geo-fallback uses a deterministic provider selection algorithm (region-preferred -> allowed-pool -> explicit-escrow with audit event); audit redaction shim removes configurable PII fields but injects residency tags and HMAC anchors for non-repudiation. Added docs, examples, and e2e coverage. Telemetry: kms_fallback_count and audit_redaction_count metrics added.
release_notes: Security: Add RBACv2 attribute-filter pass (opt-in per namespace) to prevent unsafe operator claim leakage. Reliability: Add KMS geo-fallback middleware that routes key ops to approved regional providers with explicit audit events. Compliance: Audit redaction shim strips PII while preserving residency metadata and HMAC anchors for legal verification. Metrics and docs included.
